title: Stop updating the url at every keystroke, only update after thresold
body:
This is triggering bad behavior on chrome osx and also sometime chrome linux.

There's some good overhead because updating the url seems to not be DOM or V8 but browser related. So if the browser implemented it in a bad way then it fails.

You can ask @olance or @seafoox for visual proof of this slowness, that's impressive.

See #827

On a UX side in the end updating the url at every keystroke does introduce a rendering noise were two very different part of the interface changes: the url bar, the instant search interface. After disabling it to test the performance I found it less intrusive to only update it after the thresold.

Thoughts?
